title: SDK: unified call-adapter + local schema coercion for function/tool invocation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: SDK users across Python/TypeScript/Go need a consistent, ergonomic way to declare function/tool schemas, validate invocation payloads locally, and consume streamed function outputs with sensible retries and fallbacks. Existing per-language guidance diverges (pydantic vs AJV vs gojsonschema), and streaming return semantics are brittle when tools emit partial JSON or newline-delimited chunks.

Goal: Implement a portable "call-adapter" helper and validation shim in each SDK that: (1) exposes a single surface for declaring functions/tools (name, json-schema, metadata), (2) validates and coerces input args locally before making network calls, returning helpful errors early, (3) supports streaming function responses with reassembly and partial-object merging, (4) includes retry policy hooks for idempotent tool calls and graceful fallbacks to non-function invocation when models lack function-calling, and (5) provides copy-paste examples for Python/TS/Go and tests for edge-cases (partial json, extra fields, null coercion).
acceptance_criteria: call-adapter API implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with identical method names and parameters
local validation uses pydantic (Python), AJV + TypeScript types (TS), gojsonschema (Go) and returns normalized typed objects or clear validation errors
streaming helper can be used as async iterator (Python/TS) or channel-based reader (Go) and reconstructs function outputs from chunked JSON/NDJSON reliably
retry hooks available with configurable idempotency flags and backoff strategy documented
end-to-end tests that simulate partial/chunked tool responses, invalid args, and model fallback to non-function mode
docs/snippets included in SDK README and Console quickstart template
notes: Decided to validate/coerce locally rather than relying solely on server-side errors to reduce noisy network round-trips and surface errors with better stack traces.
We will publish a canonical JSON Schema v2020-12 shape for function args. Language-specific runtimes map that schema into native validators (pydantic BaseModel generation, AJV compile, gojsonschema).
For TypeScript we will ship generated d.ts helper via an optional codegen step (cli: redwood gen-functions) so that consumers can get compile-time types that align with runtime AJV checks.

Streaming behavior: adopt a two-layer strategy: (A) streaming token reader that exposes raw token deltas, and (B) a reassembly layer aware of JSON partials which attempts to merge partial objects until valid JSON is produced. If reassembly fails after timeout, emit an error event with raw text payload for debugging.

Retries: SDK exposes a 'retry_policy' param on call-adapter. Default: idempotent=false (no retries) for user-defined tools. For explicitly marked idempotent tools (metadata.idempotent=true) default backoff: exponential, 3 attempts, jitter. Retry hooks allow logging/metrics integration.

Fallbacks: if server responds with model that does not support function-calling, SDK will optionally translate to 'structured-prompt' invocation, passing the declared schema as a hint and coercing the top-level model output into the expected shape using the local validator. This is opt-in via 'allow_structured_fallback' flag.

Design trade-off: we opted to implement local coercion (e.g., stringify numbers->ints, coerce 'true'/'false' strings to booleans per schema) but not aggressive heuristics (no deep fuzzy parsing of free text into complex nested structures) to avoid accidental data corruption.

Security: validators run on client side only; we added a lint rule in TS to discourage embedding secrets in function schemas. Security review flagged potential leakage vectors when schemas contain PII in examples — recommending doc guidance.

Interop: call-adapter metadata includes 'compatibility' fields to signal server-supported parameter encoding (json, ndjson, newline-delimited json-chunks) so we can route to appropriate streaming parser.
Performance: local validation adds ~1-3ms overhead for typical small arg objects; microbenchmarks attached in PRs.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): prototype reassembly algorithm using Python async iterator and sample streamed NDJSON payloads. Validate failure modes and timeouts.
Phase 2 (Core SDK, 2 weeks): implement call-adapter + validators in Python and TypeScript, include unit tests and small integration test against mock server. Add retry hooks and idempotency metadata.
Phase 3 (Go port + QA, 1.5 weeks): implement Go helper with channel-based streaming reader, compile-time schema checks in examples, run fuzz tests for partial chunks.
Phase 4 (Docs + Samples, 3 days): write cross-language examples, add migration guide for users of old function helpers, update Console quickstart.
Phase 5 (Staging rollout, 1 week): enable behind feature flag in SDK release, monitor errors and performance, collect developer feedback, iterate.
Phase 6 (GA): remove feature flag after two weekly cycles of telemetry showing <0.5% error increase and no major regressions.
qa_steps: Unit tests for validator failure paths (missing required, wrong type, extra fields when additionalProperties=false)
Integration test: mock server emits chunked JSON object across 6 tokens, SDK must reassemble and produce final parsed object
Retry test: mark tool idempotent and force transient 5xx from server, assert SDK retries with backoff and emits metrics hooks
Fallback test: simulate model without function-calling — SDK should, when allow_structured_fallback=true, parse free-text output into validated object or return structured validation error
Fuzz test: random byte-splitting across boundary conditions for streaming reader in Go and Python
example_snippets:
Python (sync/async)
from redwood import CallAdapter
from pydantic import BaseModel

class SummarizeArgs(BaseModel):
    text: str
    max_lines: int = 3

adapter = CallAdapter()
fn = adapter.register_function('summarize', schema=SummarizeArgs.schema(), idempotent=True)

# async streaming consumption
async for chunk in fn.call_stream({'text': long_text}):
    print(chunk)  # chunk is incremental text until final JSON is reassembled

# sync convenience call
res = fn.call({'text': 'hello world', 'max_lines': 2})
# res is validated SummarizeArgs response model or raises ValidationError
comments: 2025-11-13 - Asha: Kickoff completed with SDK leads. Identified AJV/pydantic/gojsonschema as the runtimes to standardize on. Agreed on minimal coercion rules.
2025-11-20 - Marco: Spike results attached in PR #412 show reassembly success on >95% of sampled NDJSON splits; edgecases logged.
2025-12-01 - Nina (PM): Please ensure the default retry policy is conservative. We can't have silent double-execution of non-idempotent tools. Added 'idempotent' metadata requirement for retries.
2026-01-15 - Design review (Liam): UX for streaming API looks good; suggested explicit 'on_partial' callback for Console integration which we added.

2026-02-25 - QA: Found a race in Go channel close leading to lost last chunk when server closes connection with no newline. Patch in sdk-go PR #57 addresses this by buffering final bytes before closing.
2026-03-02 - Security: Reviewed potential leakage of examples in schemas; added guidance to docs and linter warning for TS.
2026-03-08 - Marco: Merged Python and TS core adapters; Go port in review. Preparing canary release under feature flag 'call_adapter_v2'.
